stopwords_considered_and_rejected: sciences (plural) — protected by a prior documented MINESUP-E decision as a legitimate specialty differentiator; adding it would silently override that decision across all registries
matching_hardening.null_city_behavior_before: geo comparison used `normalizeGeo(region) || normalizeGeo(city)` — region always short-circuited city via `||`, so city was structurally never consulted whenever region was known (true for all 22 pilot rows). NULL/NULL itself never literally counted as a positive match (falsy `||` chain produced an empty string, treated as non-comparable), but city was silently unusable as a discriminator even once populated.
matching_hardening.null_city_behavior_after: geoAgreement(regionA, cityA, regionB, cityB) — compares city first if both known (most specific), falls back to region only if city unknown on either side, returns UNKNOWN (never a positive match) if neither known on both sides. Exported, generic across all registries.
matching_hardening.geo_conflict_tiebreak_fix: targets in explicit geo CONFLICT are excluded from the AMBIGUOUS tie-break pool whenever a non-conflicting target exists at the same overlap ratio — a target in a different city never wins or ties against one in the correct city.
matching_hardening.locality_token_double_counting_fix: a locality name already captured by the structured city/region fields is excluded from the fuzzy word-overlap ratio itself, to stop the same geographic signal being double-counted as a 'distinctive' word.
